messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have been working with R for a while, and recently I moved to
Ubuntu10.10 and installed Rkward. 

I am more or less satisfied with it, except for a few things:

- The output is a mess. In the terminal / macos R gui the output always
came out neatly in the form of a table. Bu not in rkward, making it a
nightmare to try to read out the output without first pasting it and
formatting it. It appears that each cell in the table is centered and
misaligned. 

- Output tables only occupy half of the console space, and making the
output unnecessarily long and impossible to work out for dataframes
with more than 5 - 6 columns. 

- Tweaking the color scheme of the editor, I made the huge mistake of
inadvertedly pressing the " use KDE colors", and now all color schemas
are exactly the same. There was no way to re-set the color schemas.
Removing and re-installing rkward didn't do anything, nor removing
configuration files or editing them to re=set the colors. The only
alternative was to completely reinstall KDE. This is a pretty annoying
behaviour, especially because pressing that button should not have any
effect on the pre-existing color schemes, nor should it change them

Looking forward to any comments and solutions

messages.body_plain:
hi daniel,

thanks for your interest in using RKWard! first things first: it appears you 
are not subscribed to this list -- you might lose replies because they usually 
only go to the list. you might like to subscribe for the time being.

Am Dienstag, 8. November 2016, 20:02:04 CET schrieb Daniel P.:
> I have been working with R for a while, and recently I moved to
> Ubuntu10.10 and installed Rkward.

is that a typo? do you mean ubuntu 16.10? there is no more support for 10.10 
for many years now.

could you please give us some more info on your system (ideally the output of 
rk.sessionInfo(), at least version numbers of KDE, R and RKWard)?

> - The output is a mess.

can you give a specific example (R code)? i've never had any issues with the 
consle output, it looks just like any other R console, except for extra syntax 
highlighting etc.

> - Output tables only occupy half of the console space, and making the
> output unnecessarily long and impossible to work out for dataframes
> with more than 5 - 6 columns.

you can customize the width of the output in settings -> configure RKWard -> R 
backend.

> - Tweaking the color scheme of the editor, I made the huge mistake of
> inadvertedly pressing the " use KDE colors", and now all color schemas
> are exactly the same.

if that is the case, this is more likely a bug in kate (katepart), the editor 
we're using in RKWard.

> There was no way to re-set the color schemas.
> Removing and re-installing rkward didn't do anything, nor removing
> configuration files or editing them to re=set the colors. The only
> alternative was to completely reinstall KDE.

are you suggesting that a user specific configuration changed settings system 
wide for all users? that would be a major flaw. but like i said, we didn't 
invent an editor ourselves but are embedding katepart, so there's not too much 
we can tell you about this.


viele grüße :: m.eik

messages.body_plain:
hi julian,

Am Donnerstag, 24. November 2016, 20:56:20 CET schrieb Julian Highley:
> As you suggest the front end seems to be compiled for 3.2.5 and my version
> of R is 3.3.1.

ok, that explains it.

> Do I need to compile RKWard from source to resolve or is there an easier
> way?

it's a bit curious how the distribution packages could become so mixed up. are 
you using standard distribution packages for both R and RKWard? if so, you 
should probably file a bug report (to the ubuntu deveolpers) because this 
combination simply can't work for ubuntu users. they'd need to recompile the 
package.

anyway, i'd recommend to switch to a) CRAN packages of R:
 https://cran.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu/README.html
and b) our PPA package of RKWard:
 https://launchpad.net/~rkward-devel/+archive/ubuntu/rkward-stable-cran
this makes sure you always get the latest stable release of both R and RKWard 
and they're both in sync, dependency-wise.

there's also some alternative PPAs, if you're feeling lucky ;-)
 https://launchpad.net/~rkward-devel
you'd always need one for CRAN R if you're using its packages, obviously.

in addition to that (and not related to your problem), i personally am very 
happy with the C2D4U (CRAN to deb for ubuntu) packages and prefer them over 
installing R packages from source:
 https://launchpad.net/~marutter/+archive/ubuntu/c2d4u
most packages that are available on CRAN are also available as a debian 
package here. they're usually called "r-cran-<package name>" then.


viele grüße :: m.eik
